items.headline: Microsoft and Alphabet report Wednesday Oct 28 and Amazon Thursday Oct 29, with consensus EPS of $4.71, $2.94 and $2.01
items.why: After last week's sell-off on AI spending, these three cloud reports are the next hard test of whether data-center outlays are turning into revenue.

sources.title: Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon Lead the Earnings Week of October 26

items.headline: Meta beat on revenue ($64.6B) and EPS but fell 7% after a $2.12B free-cash-flow outflow and $34.91B of Q3 AI capex; Nvidia -4%, AMD -8%, Micron -6% the same day
items.why: Investors are now punishing cash burn rather than rewarding beats, so capex guidance matters more than headline results this earnings season.

items.headline: Western Digital posts adjusted EPS of $4.64 against $4.11 expected on revenue of $4.38B, up 55% year on year
items.why: Storage demand from AI data centers is still showing up in reported numbers, a counterpoint to the spending worries hitting chip stocks.

items.headline: Korea's Kospi is nearly 20% lower this month and fell another 1.1% on Monday, with Goldman Sachs cutting its 12-month target by 25%
items.why: Korea's index is dominated by memory-chip makers, so its slide shows the AI hardware de-rating spreading well beyond US markets.

items.headline: Bitcoin slips below $80,000 on Monday, trading near $79,540 (-1.5% in 24 hours), while Ether falls to about $2,302 (-2.5%)
items.why: Losing the round-number level after a weekend of tight trading shows sellers still in control despite no new crypto-specific bad news.

sources.title: Crypto Price Analysis, BTC, ETH, HYPE, QNT and ICP, October 26

items.headline: Spot Bitcoin ETFs took in more than $1B over three sessions, yet price fell from $84,500-84,800 toward $81,000 as $436M of mostly long positions were liquidated
items.why: ETF buying is being absorbed by heavy selling around $84,000-85,000, so inflows alone are not enough to lift price while equities and geopolitics weigh.

sources.title: Daily Crypto Price Analysis - October 23, 2026: Bitcoin, Ethereum and Market Trends

items.headline: Bitcoin ends the week at $80,797, down 1.0%, with $80,400 and $79,700 named as nearby support
items.why: The weekly loss was small next to gold's 4% drop, but Monday's move already sits below both of those levels.

sources.title: Forex and Crypto Forecast October 26-30, 2026: Fed, ECB and BoJ Decisions

items.headline: Odds of a Fed hike at Wednesday's meeting have collapsed to about 7-8% from about 52% a week earlier, while a December hike is priced at 80-90%
items.why: The market has pushed the tightening out by one meeting rather than cancelling it, so the press conference tone on December will drive yields.

sources.title: Forex and Crypto Forecast October 26-30, 2026: Fed, ECB and BoJ Decisions

items.headline: Busy central-bank week: ECB likely holds Thursday, BoJ decides Friday, Bank of Canada is priced for a hike, and a November Bank of England hike remains the base case with UK CPI at 3.5%
items.why: Several central banks are leaning toward tighter policy at once because of energy pass-through, which keeps pressure on global bond yields.

items.headline: US 10-year yield climbs back to about 5% on Friday as one-year inflation expectations rise to 4.7%; France's bond spread widens to 170 bp, its widest since 2011
items.why: Oil-driven inflation fears are reversing the week's bond rally, and stress in French debt adds a European risk premium on top.

items.headline: Concern over the debt hyperscalers have taken on for AI infrastructure, plus shifting midterm-election odds, are weighing on US stocks
items.why: When the AI story becomes a credit story, weakness can spread from tech into lenders and the wider market, as Friday's broad decline showed.

items.headline: Brent settles at $116.72 on Friday, its highest since April 29, and WTI at $103.27 after Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites
items.why: Crude at these levels feeds straight into the inflation expectations that are keeping rate hikes priced and pressuring stocks and gold.

items.headline: Brent eases 1.6% to $114.88 on Monday as Qatari mediators in Tehran work with the US to calm regional tensions
items.why: Part of the oil price is a geopolitical premium that can fall quickly on diplomacy, so headlines on an Iran deal now move crude day to day.

items.headline: Comex gold posts its steepest weekly drop since June, over 4%, and silver falls more than 5% to settle below $55 for the first time since November 2025
items.why: Rising oil and Fed-hike pricing plus a strong dollar are outweighing safe-haven demand, so precious metals are trading on real yields, not fear.

sources.title: Commodities Weekly Insights 26th October 2026 by Axis Securities Ltd

items.headline: Comex copper ends the week down close to 1% as rising LME inventories ease physical tightness
items.why: Easing stock tightness takes away a support that had kept copper firm while other metals fell, even as long-term electrification demand stays intact.

sources.title: Commodities Weekly Insights 26th October 2026 by Axis Securities Ltd

items.headline: S&P 500 closes at 7,623 on Friday, sitting on the lower edge of the roughly 7,620-7,800 range it has held since August
items.why: That edge is the neckline of a short-term head-and-shoulders pattern, so whether it holds this week separates a range from a breakdown toward the July lows near 7,400.

items.headline: Chip ETF SOXX fell 6.62% Thursday and touched its 200-day moving average at $473.39; SOX is down 15% on the month
items.why: The 200-day average is the line between a pullback and a trend break, and it held on the first test as chips steadied on Friday.

items.headline: Bitcoin's four-hour candle closes at $79,489.60, below its lower Bollinger band; a daily close below $79,120.80 would confirm loss of the weekend floor, with the Sept 8 low at $77,609.40 next
items.why: The weekend range has given way intraday, so the daily close against $79,120.80 decides whether the decline extends toward the September low.

sources.title: Crypto Price Analysis, BTC, ETH, HYPE, QNT and ICP, October 26

items.headline: Gold ends the week near $4,010, down 4.2%, just above support at $3,975 with resistance at $4,030
items.why: Gold is holding just above the $4,000 area after its worst week since June, so $3,975 is the level that decides whether the selling deepens.
